2026-11-17.title: Tuesday after the Sunday of the Message to Zechariah
2026-11-17.verse: And just then some people were carrying a paralyzed man lying on a bed. When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, “Take heart, son; your sins are forgiven.”
theo: Paul compares God's people to an olive tree. Some natural branches were broken off; the Gentiles, a wild olive shoot, were grafted in to share “the rich root”. So he warns: “do not boast over the branches… it is not you that support the root, but the root that supports you.” We stand by faith and by grace alone, and God can graft back in those who were cut off. Humility, not pride, is the right response to being included.

Friends carry a paralysed man to Jesus. Seeing their faith, Jesus first says what no one expected: “Take heart, son; your sins are forgiven.” The scribes call it blasphemy. So Jesus heals the man's body too, “so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins.” The crowds glorify God “who had given such authority to human beings”: the authority that Christ still exercises through his Church in Confession.
outline: “Take heart, son; your sins are forgiven.”
live: Pray by name for someone who cannot pray for themselves.
Plan a confession before the Christmas fast begins on 1 December.
2026-11-17.prayer: Lord Jesus, you saw the faith of friends and forgave the paralysed man. Forgive our sins, heal our weakness, and keep us humble branches on your living tree. Amen.

quick: Friends' faith brought the paralytic to Jesus.
We are grafted in by grace; the root supports us.
2026-11-17.question: Whom can I carry to Jesus by my prayer?

homily: Dear friends, Paul compares God's people to an olive tree. Some natural branches were broken off; the Gentiles, a wild olive shoot, were grafted in to share the rich root. So he warns: do not boast over the branches; it is not you that support the root, but the root that supports you (Romans 11:17–18).

In the Gospel some people bring to Jesus a paralysed man lying on a bed. Seeing their faith, Jesus says: take heart, son; your sins are forgiven. And so that they may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins, he heals him (Matthew 9:2–6). The faith of others carried him.

We too have been carried by the faith of others: our parents, our ancestors, the tradition of the St Thomas Christians. Today let us carry someone: a sick person, someone weary in faith, bringing them to Jesus in prayer. Amen.
kids: Children, friends carried a sick man to Jesus. Today pray for someone who is sick!

intro: Faith that carries, grace that grafts.
